key_insights: Defines the main application timing options: Early Action (non-binding, apply anywhere), Restrictive/Single-Choice Early Action (non-binding but limits other early applications), Early Decision (binding, one school only), Rolling Admissions, and Regular Decision.
Explains that Early Decision 1 and Early Decision 2 differ only in application deadline, not in bindingness or process.
Notes that applying early can raise a college's yield rate (percentage of admits who enroll), which is one reason schools favor filling large shares of the class through early rounds.

Advises students to self-check whether their GPA/scores/activities are competitive for a school's applicant pool before applying early there, since colleges may prefer to admit unknown later applicants over a weaker early one.

Points out that Early Decision commitments are enforced through an honor-based signed agreement (student, parent, counselor) rather than being a legal contract, and that a school will only release a student from ED if they cannot afford the cost.
Warns that applying ED to more than one school simultaneously is effectively unworkable because the counselor's signed agreement restricts sending transcripts to only one school.
States that if deferred from an early round, the application converts into the regular decision pool without penalty, and students remain free to apply elsewhere.
